pageCache.pageTitle: Love of Reading and Social & Cultural Development | Rowlands Castle St John's Church of England Controlled Primary School
pageCache.text:
Love of Reading and Social & Cultural Development
Through our guided reading and Monthly Book Clubs, we are trying to promote a love of reading but also, a love of reading about other faiths, cultures and experiences that might be different to our own.
We want children to have access to different fiction and non-fiction texts that teach them about the wider world and experiences of other people. We want children to reflect and celebrate everyone’s uniqueness and differing experiences.
Black History Month 2024
This year, all children will be exploring the writing of Floella Benjamin who grew up in Trinidad and moved to London as part of the Windrush Generation.
To bring the story alive, we invited Graham - a local saxophone player - in to school to perform for the children. The saxophone is referenced in the story and this performance really helps children to be immersed in the text.
Our School
Spirituality
Courageous Advocacy
saxophone performance.MOV
A Prayer for Black History Month
Compassionate God, who sent Jesus Christ to deliver us from all manner of injustices and inequalities, create in us new hearts and enlarged visions, to see the image of God in every person irrespective of background, race and ethnicity.
May we be generous in our love of others as we work towards ending racism and injustice; creating communities of human flourishing, through Jesus Christ your Son our Lord, who is alive and reigns with you, in the unity of the Holy Spirit, one God, now and for ever. Amen.
A selection of guided reading work for Black History Month
We have focused on black artists from around the world and looked at and celebrated their influence.
Year 6 were inspired by the culture, people and wildlife of the Caribbean.
Year 5 looked at the Windrush ship
We are developing our library to promote more books from different cultures and to celebrate all that makes us special.
We did an Amazon Wish List and are very thankful to parents/carers who donated books from our list.

pageCache.text:
Peripatetic Music Lessons
Peripatetic Music Tuition
At Rowlands Castle St John's we are very fortunate to be able to organise instrumental tuition on a variety of different musical instruments which we purchase through the Hampshire Music Service. We offer Piano, Guitar, Violin, Cornet, Trumpet, Clarinet, Saxophone and Flute to Years 1 - 6.
The termly cost for music tuition is £106.
However, if parents wish to pay for a full year at a discounted cost it is £280 for tuition.
Although this is organised on an annual basis for the Academic year then there can sometimes be a possibility of starting within the year if there are any spaces. Please contact the school office if your child is interested in this tuition.

pageCache.text:
British Values
British Values Statement
Through our promotion of Christian and British values we believe that we are able to equip children with the understanding, attitudes and values necessary to be able to make a positive difference in the world as they progress through life.
The Government emphasises that schools are required to ensure that key ‘British Values’ are taught in all UK schools. The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy.
The five British Values are:
• Individual liberty
• Tolerance of those of different faiths and beliefs
